_comment: Differences from the published 1.5.5 that the OWNER has accepted, each with a rationale and a kind:
improvement  additive or strictly better; a 1.5.5 client/operator keeps working unchanged
A matching cell reports as ACCEPTED in its own column — never as a silent pass — so a later change
to the same surface still shows. `cells` are id regexes; `classes` limits the acceptance to those
divergence classes (a status or usage change on an 'improvement' entry is still red).
Zero UNACCEPTED divergences is the ship gate.

An entry with `transform: {candidate: [[regex, replacement], ...]}` is line-precise: the candidate's stderr/body text is rewritten before the diff, so only that token is forgiven; the cell reports ACCEPTED, never PASS.
breaking     a deliberate change named in the 1.6.0 CHANGELOG (`changelog` field required) — the ONLY kind that may accept a `status` or `effects.usage` class
The differ refuses any entry that accepts `status` or `effects.usage` without kind=breaking and a `changelog` field, and any entry with neither `cells` nor `classes` (a total blanket).

EVERY entry, improvement or breaking, owes a `changelog` line that appears verbatim in CHANGELOG.md (ARCHITECTURE.md's owner rule accepts an improvement 'named in the CHANGELOG' too), or an explicit `"changelog": null` with a `changelog_reason`; a breaking entry may never waive. scripts/changelog-register-check.sh is the gate.

accepted.changelog: Every error and warning line carries a diagnostic code.
accepted.rationale: 1.6.0 prefixes every [error]/[warn]/warning: stderr line with a diagnostic code (BUSBAR-NNNN:) and every boot log line with diag=BUSBAR-NNNN; the text after the code is byte-identical to 1.5.5.

accepted.changelog: The jemalloc background-purge line is `[info]` on macOS
accepted.rationale: On macOS the jemalloc background-thread line is [info] with an explanation instead of 1.5.5's [warn]; same fallback behaviour.

candidate: ^\[info\] jemalloc background purge thread unavailable on this target \((.*?)\) — EXPECTED on macOS, which has no background-thread mallctl; busbar's idle-purge fallback keeps RSS returning to idle after a load burst$
[warn] could not enable jemalloc background purge thread (\1); enabling busbar's idle purge fallback so RSS still returns to idle after a load burst

accepted.changelog: One new `/metrics` series on a 1.5.5 config:
accepted.rationale: One additive /metrics series on a 1.5.5 config: busbar_metering_pending_coalesced_total (write-behind overflow sentinel). No 1.5.5 series changed.

accepted.changelog: Admin views gained fields; none changed.
accepted.rationale: Hook views gain fires_at/groups/phase; the overlay-section 404 lists the new sections; openapi.json adds the mcp/a2a endpoints. Every 1.5.5 field is unchanged. SPLIT 2026-09-05 (round-3 audit): effects.readback moved out of this improvement entry into F-011r. effects.readback is now a MONEY class (diff-cells.py rates it 10: it is the proof that the write the cell made actually persisted, and as what), and the readback half is not purely additive — the hook view's always-null `at` field is REMOVED in favour of fires_at, which is a declared breaking change and needs a changelog line.

accepted.id: F-011r hook write readback: `at` gives way to `fires_at`
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 parity triage; split out 2026-09-05 (round-3 audit)
accepted.rationale: The follow-up GET a hook write's cell performs reads the same hook view the GET cells read: it gains fires_at/groups/phase and LOSES the always-null `at` field. The additive half is F-011's; the removal is a declared 1.6.0 break named in the CHANGELOG's rewritten-spellings paragraph, so the readback class it moves is registered here as kind=breaking rather than folded into an improvement. Scoped to exactly the four cells that HAVE an effects.readback in the golden (admin.ops|PostHooks|ok, |PutHooksName|ok, |PatchHooksNameSettings|ok, |DeleteHooksName|ok); admin.ops|PostHooks|if-match-stale and every hooks|* cell record no readback at all. The readback's status and path are unchanged in all four — only the view's field set moves.
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Changed: the always-null `at` field on the hook view gives way to `fires_at` (rewritten for you by --migrate-config)
Validation messages know the new keys.
accepted.rationale: The new token limit metrics appear in a limit's expected-one-of list; reserved-name / credential-mode / unknown-member sentences rephrased; protocol list reordered. Same refusal, same exit code. NARROWED 2026-09-05 (the plane-key-lift fix): the top-level plane-key row dropped — the TOP-LEVEL expected-one-of list no longer includes the plane keys, because the 1.6.0-additive keys are lifted off the document before the frozen 1.5.5-shaped parse. That cell is byte-identical to 1.5.5 now and needs no acceptance.

accepted.changelog: a plugin download failure quotes the HTTP client's current error text
accepted.rationale: The plugin download failure quotes the HTTP client's newer error text (connect error) for the same refusal. NARROWED 2026-09-05 (the plane-key-lift fix): the two neutrality unknown-key cells dropped — NEUT-U-top's top-level list and NEUT-U-auth's auth: list are byte-identical to 1.5.5 again, because the 1.6.0-additive keys (the plane sections, and auth.policy) are lifted off the document before the frozen 1.5.5-shaped parse. Neither cell has a divergence left to waive. WIDENED 2026-09-05 (A10b): BOOT-W24's `plugins.fetch: miss on reload` warning quotes the SAME reqwest connect-error text change on the SAME download-failure path (`error sending request for url (...)` -> `client error (Connect): tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 61)`); its `diag=BUSBAR-6001` prefix is D-1 (already covered) and reaches this class only because both fire on the same line.

accepted.changelog: `--help` documents `-c`/`--config` and `--providers`; `--version` prints a second line.
accepted.rationale: --help documents the new -c/--providers flags; --version prints a second build-profile line. documented|readme|env-launch (PB-71) drives the same --version path under BUSBAR_CONFIG and hits the identical second line.

accepted.id: S-1 bedrock text blocks carry no contentBlockStart
accepted.changelog: Bedrock text blocks no longer open with an empty `contentBlockStart`.
accepted.rationale: Spec fidelity: on the AWS ConverseStream wire a text block starts with its first contentBlockDelta; contentBlockStart is emitted only for tool-use blocks. 1.5.5 emitted an empty contentBlockStart for text; 1.6.0 matches AWS. Owner rule: maximum spec compliance wins over 1.5.5 bytes.

accepted.changelog: Responses API streams carry the lifecycle frames the spec declares:
accepted.rationale: Spec fidelity: the Responses API stream includes response.content_part.added / response.output_text.done / response.content_part.done with contiguous sequence_number; 1.5.5 omitted them. Owner rule: maximum spec compliance wins over 1.5.5 bytes.

accepted.changelog: a non-2xx records the breaker outcome by status class, honouring the upstream `Retry-After` as the cooldown floor, and emits the upstream-failure series
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: A non-2xx on a fallback/least-bad/queue hop now records the breaker outcome exactly as the primary hop does (per status class, honouring the upstream Retry-After as the cooldown floor, with the upstream-failure series emitted) instead of a class-less degraded transient with no Retry-After. The client still receives the relayed upstream error; only the breaker bookkeeping and metrics changed.

accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: An auth/billing hard-down on a fallback/least-bad/queue hop now trips the lane in every breaker cell and, for busbar's own lane credential, answers with the ingress-native auth-failure envelope — the same rule the primary hop applies. Previously the degraded hop relayed the upstream 401 body verbatim and recorded nothing, leaving the dead lane Closed.
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Improvements: a fallback hop refused upstream is answered in the ingress-native auth-failure envelope and recorded on the breaker
a client-fault 4xx bumps the lane's `client_fault` counter
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: A client-fault 4xx served through a fallback/least-bad hop now bumps the lane's client_fault observability counter as the primary hop does. No breaker penalty either way; the relayed response is unchanged.

accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: OWNER DECISION: bill them. A streaming request served through a fallback/least-bad/queue hop to an OpenAI Chat Completions lane now has stream_options.include_usage injected upstream exactly as a primary hop does, so the trailing usage chunk arrives and the key is billed its real tokens (previously zero). The client-facing stream is unchanged for a client that did not opt in (the injected chunk is stripped at the framing seam); an opted-in client now receives its usage chunk on the fallback hop too. CHANGELOG 1.6.0: 'Fallback-pool and least-bad streams to OpenAI Chat Completions lanes are now metered (previously billed zero tokens).' The egress record shows the injected stream_options.include_usage on the fallback hop.
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Improvements: fallback-lane streams are now billed
a pool member's `attempt_timeout_ms` override is honoured
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: The pool-member attempt_timeout_ms override is now honoured on fallback/least-bad hops (the degraded path used only the lane-level value). The cap can only fire earlier where an operator set a tighter member override.

accepted.changelog: a transport error emits the same upstream-failure and failover series
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: A transport error (connect refused / reset / timeout) on a fallback/least-bad/queue hop now emits the same upstream-failure and failover series the primary hop emits. Breaker recording and the client response are unchanged.

accepted.changelog: A Bedrock `Converse` response always carries `metrics`.
accepted.rationale: The Converse output shape requires metrics; 1.5.5's same-dialect passthrough dropped it. 1.6.0 always carries it (latencyMs is timing and normalized).

accepted.changelog: An Anthropic response carries the members its published schema requires.
accepted.rationale: Anthropic's published Message / stream-event schemas mark stop_details, container, citations, the cache and service_tier usage members, output_tokens_details and server_tool_use required; 1.5.5 omitted them. 1.6.0 emits the spec's null/zero defaults or the carried value.

accepted.changelog: A chat completion's `logprobs` object carries `refusal`.
accepted.rationale: choices[].logprobs and message.refusal are required by the published chat schema; null when the backend carried none.

accepted.changelog: A Responses object carries the members its published schema requires.
accepted.rationale: The Response object's required members (created_at, error, incomplete_details, instructions, tools, tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls, metadata, temperature, top_p, part logprobs, usage details) are emitted with spec defaults or carried values.

accepted.changelog: `openapi.json` describes the MCP and A2A endpoints
accepted.rationale: openapi.json adds the mcp/a2a endpoints; every 1.5.5 path and schema is unchanged (a dedicated cell pins info.version). The document also gains a Vary header and reports the binary's true version in info.version (1.5.5 shipped a stale 1.5.4).

accepted.changelog: A `stream: true` request on the Responses door is answered as a stream.
accepted.rationale: A stream: true request on the Responses door is served as text/event-stream with the ResponseStreamEvent sequence; 1.5.5 answered the same-dialect case with a buffered JSON body. Metered identically (250 cents / 18 tokens). The buffered 1.5.5 body carried a synthesized content-length with no transfer-encoding; the SSE body is chunked, so the normalizer's header-shape rule fires where it did not before (norm.rules) -- a byproduct of the same content-type change, not a separate behavior.

accepted.id: E7-1 non-Responses doors stream when the backend is Responses-shaped
accepted.changelog: Every door streams when the routed lane is Responses-shaped.
accepted.rationale: A stream: true request whose routed lane is Responses-shaped is now served as text/event-stream carrying the ingress door's own translated stream frames (Cohere v2 SSE, Gemini's SSE framing, OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE); 1.5.5 answered it as a buffered application/json body regardless of the door that received it. The Anthropic- and Bedrock-door cells for the same egress already carry this fix under S-4's and S-1's broader per-door wildcards; this entry covers the three doors (Cohere, Gemini, OpenAI chat) whose own required-member registrations (S-5; none was needed for Cohere/Gemini, which had zero required-member violations) did not include the ok_stream outcome. Metered identically (250 cents / 18 tokens).

accepted.id: S-8 streamed usage carries the same attribution buckets as buffered
accepted.changelog: A streamed response's `usage` carries the same attribution buckets as a buffered one.
accepted.rationale: NARROWED 2026-09-05 (round-3 audit): was `^llm\|[a-z_]+\|[a-z_]+\|request\|ok_stream$`, which forgave a body change on EVERY streamed llm cell (32 of them) when the fix can only move the cells whose upstream actually reports an attribution sub-bucket on the streamed path. In this harness that is exactly the six `<door>|responses` cells: mock-upstream.py's /v1/responses is the only dialect whose usage object carries populated sub-buckets (input_tokens_details.cached_tokens / cache_write_tokens, output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens); anthropic_stream, openai_chat_stream, gemini_stream, cohere_stream and bedrock_stream all send the totals with every sub-bucket null or absent, so no other ok_stream cell has a bucket to gain. `llm|responses|responses|request|ok_stream` is the same-protocol A-tap half of the fix; the other five are the shared trailing-usage fold half. If a fixture ever starts sending sub-buckets on another dialect's stream, add that cell here explicitly rather than restoring the wildcard. ORIGINAL RATIONALE: A stream's usage object now reports every per-dialect attribution sub-bucket the provider sent (reasoning tokens, the two Anthropic cache-creation TTL tiers and its web-search/service-tier pair, the four OpenAI audio and predicted-outputs slices, Gemini's tool-use prompt slice, Cohere's separately-metered billed_units trio), instead of reporting them only when the same request was made with stream:false. 1.5.5 carried NO sub-buckets on either path, so nothing a 1.5.5 client read has changed value or disappeared — the buckets are additive members that were absent before; 1.6.0 recovered them on the buffered path and this closes the streamed half of the same gap, so the two answers for one request finally agree. The totals are untouched: billable_tokens ignores the whole attribution struct. CAVEAT for a future re-record: Cohere's billed_units trio is the one bucket that is NOT a slice of the totals — to_token_usage lets billed_input/billed_output win over the raw counts — so a Cohere backend that reports billed_units on a STREAM will move that stream's ledgered figures to the same numbers its buffered twin already ledgers. No recorded cell exercises it (the oracle mock sends no billed_units on a stream), so this entry accepts `body` only; should a fixture ever start sending it, the effects.usage delta must be re-registered as kind=breaking with a CHANGELOG line rather than folded in here.

accepted.id: M-1 refund reaches the cell the charge reached
accepted.changelog: A failed request's flat fee is refunded even when its window rolled under it.
accepted.rationale: NARROWED 2026-09-05 (round-3 audit): was `^(billing|limits)\|`, which forgave a body or header change on EVERY billing and limits cell — i.e. it would have waived a WRONG BILLING FIGURE in any of those response bodies, the exact class of bug this register exists to surface. The entry's own rationale already states the served change is a no-op on every cell the oracle records (no scripted cell drives a window straddle), so the correct scope is the ONE future cell that will drive it: billing|key-usage|refund-across-window (defined SKIP-able in cells.json; the recorder owes it once the mock can drive a concurrent window roll). Until that cell is recorded this entry matches nothing, which is the point. ORIGINAL RATIONALE: A request pinned to window M whose charge landed in place on a cell a concurrent admission had already rolled to M+1 now has its flat per-request fee refunded from that same cell. 1.5.5 resolved a charge on `window > cell.window_start` (charge in place on a rolled cell) but a refund on `cell.window_start == window`, so the two halves of one request could land on different cells and a failed straddling request kept its fee for the life of that window -- leaving the derived spend a budget cap reads one fee too high. refund_bucket now mirrors resolve_for_charge exactly (`cell.window_start >= window`): the refund reaches the cell the charge reached. A cell genuinely OLDER than the request's window is still a no-op under both rules. Strictly in the client's favour and only ever reachable on a boundary straddle, which no scripted oracle cell drives -- the recorded billing and limits cells are unchanged. The divergence class it WOULD produce is effects.usage, and this register's own rule reserves that class for a kind=breaking entry naming a CHANGELOG line, so if a cell ever does show it the entry must be promoted by the owner rather than widened here.

accepted.id: M-2 a mid-stream upstream failure is not billed as a completion
accepted.changelog: A stream that dies mid-flight is no longer served, and billed, as a completed one.
accepted.rationale: NARROWED 2026-09-05 (round-4 audit): was `^llm\|`, which forgave a body change on every one of the 127 recorded LLM cells -- any writer regression whose only symptom is a wrong response body would have reported PASS/ACCEPTED under this entry. The entry's own rationale states no recorded cell exercises either shape, so the honest scope is the two future cells that will (an inline `data: {"error":...}` chunk on an OpenAI-compatible stream, a terminal `finish_reason: "ERROR"` on a Cohere stream); until they are recorded this entry matches nothing. ORIGINAL RATIONALE: Two upstream mid-stream failure shapes were served, and billed, as clean successes. (1) An OpenAI-compatible backend (OpenAI, Azure, vLLM, OpenRouter) that fails AFTER its 200 headers are on the wire delivers the failure inline as a `data: {"error":{...}}` SSE chunk carrying no `choices`; the openai_chat stream reader guarded only on the [DONE] sentinel and `choices`, so the chunk decoded to nothing at all -- no IrStreamEvent::Error, so terminal_error() stayed None, the breaker recorded no fault, the partial completion was billed in full, and a cross-protocol client got balanced block-stops plus an ordinary terminator with no hint the answer was truncated. The gemini, bedrock, anthropic and openai_responses readers each already pushed an Error for their equivalent frame. (2) A Cohere stream ending on the generic infra `finish_reason: "ERROR"` decoded to IrStopReason::Error but pushed no Error event, and no other dialect's writer has a native token for that reason, so every cross-protocol writer rendered it as a success terminator (stop/end_turn) -- the same outcome by a different route. 1.5.5 had the identical gap (v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/proto/openai_chat/reader.rs read_response_events carries the same two guards and no error arm), so this is a deliberate divergence from the pin, named in the 1.6.0 CHANGELOG under Improvements. Strictly in the operator's and the client's favour: a failed request stops being charged for, and a failing lane finally trips. ERROR_TOXIC is deliberately untouched -- it maps to IrStopReason::Safety, a content-moderation refusal is a correctly-served response, and faulting a lane for one would trip the breaker on ordinary safety behaviour. No successful stream changes on any dialect. NO RECORDED CELL EXERCISES EITHER SHAPE: the oracle mock has no mock_control verb that injects an inline error chunk or a terminal ERROR finish_reason (the closest, `cut`, severs the body rather than sending an error frame), so the recorded llm family is unchanged. The divergence classes this WOULD produce on such a cell are `status` and `effects.usage`, and this register's own rule reserves both for a kind=breaking entry naming a CHANGELOG line; this entry therefore accepts `body` only, and if a fixture is ever added that drives one of these shapes the entry must be promoted by the owner rather than widened here.

accepted.id: M-3 Cohere billed_units bill the same buffered and streamed
accepted.rationale: Cohere reports usage TWICE -- a raw `usage.tokens` bucket and a separately-metered `usage.billed_units` bucket -- and billed_units is the count Cohere itself invoices the operator on. 1.5.5 read only `tokens` (its cohere reader parsed usage.tokens on both the stream and the non-stream path; billed_units was never read) and billed those. 1.6.0 lets billed_input_tokens/billed_output_tokens win over the raw totals inside IrUsage::to_token_usage, the one projection the ledger reads. This entry covers the BUFFERED arm finally reaching that same projection: chat_usage (the projection behind ChatRespHandle::billing()) had been rebuilding TokenUsage from the RAW IrUsage totals, so a single completion was billed the billed counts when streamed and the raw counts when buffered -- two different invoices for one completion, decided only by the caller's stream flag. Both arms now answer identically. No other dialect populates the billed fields, so every other backend's ledgered counts stay byte-identical to 1.5.5. The oracle's own mock sends billed_units EQUAL to tokens, so no recorded cell moves today; the entry is registered ahead of any fixture that makes them differ, which is exactly what S-8's caveat requires.
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Improvements: a Cohere backend's `usage.billed_units` is what the key is billed, on both the buffered and the streamed path

accepted.id: F-014 Bedrock totalTokens counts the cache tokens AWS counts
accepted.rationale: AWS Converse reports inputTokens as the NON-cached input only and documents the full input as inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens (its worked caching example totals 16 input + 4 output + 695 cache-write as totalTokens 715). 1.5.5's Bedrock writer derived totalTokens = inputTokens + outputTokens while emitting the two cache counts beside it as ADDITIVE siblings, so on a cache-bearing response the published parts summed PAST the published total and a consumer reading totalTokens -- the field AWS points accounting consumers at -- lost every cache token. Both write sites (the buffered Converse body and the streamed metadata frame) now publish the AWS sum. The component fields are untouched, a response with no cache activity is byte-identical to 1.5.5 (the omitted cache buckets add zero), and this is a Bedrock-INGRESS body shape only: nothing Busbar ledgers reads totalTokens, since the Bedrock reader never parses it. The oracle's mock reports no cache tokens, so no recorded cell moves today.
